minutes.headline: Sewer Commission elected officers, sought an overdue pump station scope, and held minutes pending corrections.
minutes.summary: The commission reported its new officers, a minutes clerk vacancy, and DPW pump station follow-ups, and asked for the scope report by the next meeting. It heard updates on the car wash privilege fee legal question and grease trap compliance, signed the Q1 commitment, and held back the August 22 minutes for a member to add omitted points. Items were carried to the September 12 agenda.

budget_items.what_was_said: The total for the first-quarter commitment was stated and members signed the commitment pages.
Invoices were reported for Leominster's quarterly charge and a second invoice based on flow meters.

budget_items.topic: Small water contract renewal for pump stations
budget_items.what_was_said: The renewal contract arrived and has no issues, which allows a monthly activity report to be requested.

The 380 electric car wash item, the grease trap item and Bob Proctor were put on the next agenda.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission asked that the DPW pump station scope report be sent by the September 12 meeting, where it stays on the agenda.
The commission held the August 22 minutes unapproved so a member can listen to the tape and add omitted points.
Members signed the first-quarter sewer commitment pages; no recorded votes were taken.
Grease trap compliance was put on the September 12 agenda to see whether the restaurant responds, with options discussed if it does not.
The commission reported its new officers and a minutes clerk vacancy, and confirmed the chair as liaison to the DPW.

why_it_matters: Sewer charges, pump station upkeep and enforcement of grease trap rules on restaurants all depend on follow-through from these open items, which affect sewer bills and the reliability of the system.
The car wash privilege fee question and the Leominster flow-based invoices bear on how sewer costs are shared among users, and both remain unresolved.
